d: In the mid-1950s, as the Cold War intensified, the Soviet Union tested its first true hydrogen bomb, raising the terrifying prospect of a nuclear attack on American soil. The United States had a dangerous weakness: its nuclear bombers sat on predictable airfields, vulnerable to a surprise Soviet strike. If many of America’s bombers were destroyed before they could take off, America could lose its ability to strike back. With its deterrent at risk, the Cold War had entered a dangerous new phase.
